body:
Triage (triage seat, session `session_01HXzdkKx5WjwwCTT3c7U5kB`): `finding` → `pm:queue`, type Task, `auto-adjudicated` — veto window open.

Ruling: **options 1 + 3 together.** (1) Remove the shadowed `SimpleTableRenderer` (`data-display/table.tsx`): it is unreachable on the `table` key (complex registers later and wins), has zero other consumers, and removing it changes no reachable behavior — today's authorable truth (`table` reads `data` + `columns`, not `bind`) stays exactly as it is. (3) Add a same-namespace duplicate-registration guard (registry-level loud signal or a gate test) — this defect was found by an accidental probe precisely because the registry is silent on overrides. Mechanical boundary test: no acceptance-set or public-surface change; dead-code removal + a new guard.

What is deliberately NOT ruled: whether `table` should learn `bind`. That would expand the authorable surface — if anyone wants it, it is a Feature for the maintainer, and deleting the shadowed renderer does not foreclose it (the bind-reading logic is 30 lines reconstructible from `list.tsx`/`tree-view.tsx`'s pattern). Fork clause: census docs/skills for published teaching of bind-on-`table` beyond the known #5126 case before deleting; any found ⇒ stop, inbox.

Side effect worth noting in the PR: this confirms for #5126 that no reachable table renderer reads `bind` — that doc card's direction is stable under this ruling.

Size/model suggestion: S–M, `mode:subagent`.

That holds **only if `SimpleTableRenderer` is not on `@object-ui/components`'s published export surface.** See the stop condition below.
Serial constraints cleared: nothing open touches `packages/components/src/renderers/data-display/**`. **PR5326 (#5254) merged this round** and touched `packages/components/src/renderers/form/**` — a different subtree; rebase on current `main` and re-read.

## Zone 1 — RULED (auto-adjudicated by the triage seat, veto window open)

> Ruling: **options 1 + 3 together.** (1) Remove the shadowed `SimpleTableRenderer` (`data-display/table.tsx`): it is unreachable on the `table` key (complex registers later and wins), has zero other consumers, and removing it changes no reachable behavior — today's authorable truth (`table` reads `data` + `columns`, not `bind`) stays exactly as it is. (3) Add a same-namespace duplicate-registration guard (registry-level loud signal or a gate test) — this defect was found by an accidental probe precisely because the registry is silent on overrides.
>
> What is deliberately NOT ruled: whether `table` should learn `bind`. That would expand the authorable surface — if anyone wants it, it is a Feature for the maintainer, and deleting the shadowed renderer does not foreclose it (the bind-reading logic is 30 lines reconstructible from `list.tsx`/`tree-view.tsx`'s pattern).

⛔ **Do not implement option 2.** Making `complex/table.tsx` read `bind` expands the authorable key surface and is explicitly not ruled. If your work starts trending that way, stop.

## ⛔ Two stop conditions. Either one ⇒ stop and report; do not proceed.

**(A) The ruling's own fork clause.** *"Census docs/skills for published teaching of bind-on-`table` beyond the known #5126 case before deleting; any found ⇒ stop, inbox."* Run that census and **show the commands and their output** — `content/docs/**`, `skills/**`, package READMEs. **A zero is not a reading until you counter-probe it** with a term you know is taught there (e.g. `bind` on `list`, which *is* a reachable bind reader). #5126 is the known case and does not by itself trip the clause.

**(B) The published-surface check, which the ruling assumes rather than states.** Before deleting anything, measure whether `SimpleTableRenderer` is a **named export of `@object-ui/components`'s public entry** — check the built `dist/index.d.ts` and the barrel chain, not a grep of `src/`. If it is exported, deleting it is **removal of a published capability**, which is maintainer-floor and outside an auto-adjudicated card's boundary — **stop and report**, do not proceed and do not "fix" it by leaving a deprecated stub. If it is not exported, say so with the evidence and carry on.

## Premise — re-verify on today's `main`

The card measured: two registrations of `table` in namespace `ui` (`data-display/table.tsx:76` and `complex/table.tsx:25`), with `renderers/index.ts` importing `./data-display` (line 13) before `./complex` (line 17), so the complex one registers later and wins. Its probe read `rows=0 text="NameRole"` against a 2-row binding — header, zero rows, and **no "No results." line**, which is the complex renderer's behaviour, not `SimpleTableRenderer`'s. Re-run something equivalent; the card is ~30 hours old.

## The guard (option 3) — make it catch this class, not this instance

The registry is silent when a later registration overwrites an earlier one in the same namespace. Whichever form you choose — a loud runtime signal or a gate test — it must **fail on a re-introduced duplicate**, not merely on the `table` key. Prove that: add a duplicate deliberately, watch the guard fire, remove it. Report that ablation.

⚠️ If you choose a runtime warning, check what the existing meta-less `register` deprecation warning already does so you do not add a second, differently-shaped warning channel for the same registry.

## Tests

- `table` still renders exactly as it does today — `data` + `columns`, no `bind`. **This is the "changes no reachable behavior" claim; it needs a test, not an assertion.**
- The guard fires on a same-namespace duplicate registration (the ablation above).
- Nothing else in `data-display` lost its registration in the deletion — `list` and `tree-view` (the other two `useDataScope` consumers) still register and still read `bind`.

Reverse-verify: restore the deleted file and its registration, keep the tests, **predict which go red before running**, report predicted vs observed. ⚠️ Note the awkward direction here: restoring a *shadowed* renderer may change nothing observable, which is itself the finding — if a leg is degenerate, **say so plainly rather than filling in the template**. State per leg whether a build artifact sits between the edit and the thing under test (`packages/components` is consumed through `dist` by its own consumers).

## Gates

Derive from your diff (`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is **objectstack-only**). Run vitest **from the repo root** — and note the real reason, because the guard's own header states it wrongly: it is not that a package-scoped run is refused (17 packages own a standalone `vitest.config.ts`, `packages/components` among them, and are **not** refused), it is that a package-scoped run uses **a different config than CI does**, so its green is not CI's green. Changeset required (`@object-ui/components`); `patch` or `minor`, ⛔ **never `major`**.

⛔ Do not background a long check and end your turn. ⛔ No exhaustive paginated API sweeps.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first body line `Fixes #5125`. Note in the PR body the side effect the ruling asks you to record: this confirms for **#5126** that no reachable table renderer reads `bind`, so that doc card's direction is stable. Push the branch early. Return the JSON report and post it as a comment whose first line is the literal `<!-- os-dev-report -->` marker.
